pointers.sentence: A command can be typed three ways, and all three call `execute_from_command_line` (`django/core/management/__init__.py:execute_from_command_line`).
It sets `"DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE"` to the project's settings module unless the environment has a value already, and calls the function with `sys.argv` (`django/conf/project_template/manage.py-tpl`).
`python -m django` runs Django's `__main__` module, which calls it too (`django/__main__.py`).

The utility keeps the list, and the base name of its first item as the program's name for messages; where that is `"__main__.py"` it says `"python -m django"` instead (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.__init__`).
It cannot look the name up at once, because which commands exist depends on the settings (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.execute`).

`handle_default_options` then acts on what was found: a settings module's name is written to the environment variable, and a directory is put at the front of the module search path (`django/core/management/base.py:handle_default_options`).
`get_commands` returns a dictionary from each command's name to the name of the application that provides it (`django/core/management/__init__.py:get_commands`).
It starts with Django's own commands, the modules of `django/core/management/commands/`, each entered under the name `"django.core"`.
A helper module can therefore sit beside the commands, under a name that starts with one (`django/core/management/__init__.py:find_commands`).

In a process whose installed applications change, the test framework's, a receiver of the `setting_changed` signal empties the cache whenever `"INSTALLED_APPS"` is overridden (`django/test/signals.py:update_installed_apps`).
An error raised by the import is not caught (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.fetch_command`, `django/core/management/__init__.py:load_command_class`).

Help followed by a name fetches that command, as above, and prints its parser's help (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.main_help_text`).
The subcommand version, or `--version` as the only argument, prints what `get_version` returns (`django/utils/version.py:get_version`).

The method prints the candidates for that word and exits: the names of the commands, or the options of the command already named, which it gets by fetching that command and building its parser (`django/core/management/__init__.py:ManagementUtility.autocomplete`, `extras/django_bash_completion`).
